findings.text: The decision says that the whole 0.2.0 source set lies inside the copied set, so that its absence 'refuses twice: through that binding, and through rule B's condition 4'. The 0.2.0 source set is every regular file under SOURCE_TREES (the observer's source_paths), and a tracked file there whose path has an ignored() component, such as ontokin/.env or prototypes/static_tray_v01/build/helper.py, lies in the source set but outside the copied set. The copy leaves it out, and rule B alone would admit its deletion line; only the binding refuses it ('Complete CPU source inventory differs'). The outcome is fail-closed and the decision's conclusion (no amendment) stands; P37-C24 freezes that refusal. At the declaration commit no tracked path has an ignored() component (W1's index reading). Recommendation: correct the sentence in a later record; no code change.

observations.text: The plan lists the driver's ordinary behaviour as unchanged, and its item 4 admits a correction of FZ-02 with its own controls. The decision names the one added Git start as the exception; P37-C60 and P37-C63 freeze it. The next MR attempt's start inventory must count it.

The controls keep the account's global Git files out (XDG_CONFIG_HOME). In a real run, where such files exist, Git's default global ignore file applies to the provider's ls-files --others --exclude-standard (Q-10 of MR's freeze review), and Git's default global attributes file applies to the driver's and provider's Git reads, which set no core.attributesFile (only the storage step's starts set it to /dev/null). Unchanged by W1; for the next MR freeze.

This host's Git (2.50.1, the developer tools' build) quotes a name with a space in porcelain v1, so such an uncopied path refuses here; the decision notes that some versions do not. The real-Git quoted controls use a double quote and a non-ASCII letter, which Git quotes under the default core.quotePath; the space case is frozen at the exact-line level in both forms (P37-C50 unquoted, P37-C54 quoted).
